bugs.text: The player ship never appears. startGame sets player.active = false (782) and neither startStage nor startRegularStage calls resetPlayer(); resetPlayer is only invoked at 1073 when playerRespawning is true, which is only set in losePlayerShip/capturePlayer after an active ship is lost. updatePlayer returns at 1078, so movement and firing are dead; scheduleDive (798) and fireEnemyBullet (886) bail on !player.active. Result: after the STAGE 1 intro the formation flies in and sits forever, score stays 0, no dives, no shots, no game over. All 75 s play screenshots show no player ship. The game soft-locks on stage 1 with no way back to the title except reloading.
sfxEnemyHit is defined but never called; there is no distinct 'enemy hit' sound (the Boss hit sound covers only the boss).

When a goei escort is shot during the dive it is not removed from its boss's escorts array (destroyEnemy only clears escorts when the boss dies), so the boss would still score 800/1600 after its escorts are already dead. Latent, since dives never happen.

A freed captive reaching the player while the player is already dual is silently dropped; and a freed ship docks (pendingDock) even if it was freed during a respawn, with no flight animation to the new ship. Latent.
Challenging-stage waves alternate zako/goei/boss types and boss-type enemies keep hp 2, so two hits are needed for one 100-point hit, which makes a PERFECT noticeably harder than the arcade. Latent.

summary: The code is cleanly organised (one state object, separate update and render passes, fixed-timestep loop, pre-rendered pixel sprites, a bitmap font) and nearly every Galaga system is written out: bezier entry paths in groups, sway and breathing, dives with return from the top, boss escorts, a tractor beam with capture, rescue and dual fighter, challenging stages with wave bonuses, badge denominations, extra ships and a hit-ratio results screen. But one omission kills it: nothing ever sets the player ship active at the start of a game, and every other mechanic (firing, dives, enemy fire, collisions, tractor beam, stage clear, game over) is gated on an active player. What actually plays is a title screen, a STAGE 1 card, a formation that flies in and breathes, and then nothing, forever. As delivered it looks like Galaga for eight seconds and is not a game.
